title: Complex numbers
description: Questions on complex numbers as points, conjugates and absolute value, polar form, powers, roots and quadratics.

questions.question: What is a complex number, as this chapter builds it?
options: A real number with a square root
A pair $$(a, b)$$ of real numbers, a point of the plane
A number that can't be written down
questions.explanation: Complex numbers are built as points, with a rule for multiplying them (:ref{#complex-number}).

questions.question: What is $$i^{27}$$?
questions.explanation: $$27 = 4 \cdot 6 + 3$$, and $$i^3 = -i$$ (:ref{#powers-of-i}).

questions.question: Which complex numbers square to $$-1$$?
questions.explanation: Comparing parts of $$(a + bi)^2 = -1$$ leaves only $$\pm i$$ (:ref{#square-roots-minus-one}).

questions.question: Why can you expand brackets with complex numbers as usual?
options: The rules of arithmetic are proved for them
questions.explanation: Grouping, order and distributivity are proved from the definition (:ref{#complex-arithmetic}).

questions.question: What is the conjugate of $$3 - 4i$$, and what does conjugating do to the point?
options: $$3 + 4i$$: a flip in the real axis
$$-3 - 4i$$: a flip in the imaginary axis
questions.explanation: Only the sign of the imaginary part changes (:ref{#conjugate}).

questions.question: What is $$\lvert 3 + 4i \rvert$$?
questions.explanation: $$\sqrt{9 + 16} = 5$$, the distance from $$0$$ (:ref{#complex-abs}). Not $$3 + 4$$.

questions.question: What is $$\frac{4 + 3i}{1 + 2i}$$?
questions.explanation: Multiply top and bottom by $$1 - 2i$$: $$\frac{10 - 5i}{5}$$ (:ref{#complex-inverse}). Check: $$(2 - i)(1 + 2i) = 4 + 3i$$.

questions.question: What is $$z\bar z$$ for $$z = a + bi$$?
questions.explanation: $$z\bar z = \lvert z \rvert^2$$ (:ref{#times-conjugate}), which is how division works.

questions.question: If $$\lvert z \rvert = 2$$ and $$\lvert w \rvert = 3$$, what is $$\lvert zw \rvert$$?
questions.explanation: Lengths multiply (:ref{#abs-product-complex}).

questions.question: What is $$-2 + 2i$$ in polar form?
questions.explanation: Length $$\sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt2$$, and the point is in the second quarter on the line $$y = -x$$ (:ref{#polar-form}).

questions.question: When you multiply two complex numbers, what happens to their angles?
questions.explanation: $$re^{i\theta} \cdot se^{i\varphi} = rs\,e^{i(\theta + \varphi)}$$: lengths multiply, angles add (:ref{#polar-multiply}).

questions.question: What does multiplying by $$i$$ do to a point?
options: Flips it in the real axis
Turns it a quarter turn about $$0$$
questions.explanation: $$i(x + yi) = -y + xi$$ (:ref{#multiply-by-i}). Two quarter turns make a half turn, so $$i^2 = -1$$.

questions.question: What does $$e^{i\theta}$$ mean in this chapter?
options: The number $$e$$ to a real power
questions.explanation: It is a name chosen because it obeys the exponent rule (:ref{#e-i-theta}, :ref{#polar-multiply}).

questions.question: What is $$(1 + i)^{10}$$?
questions.explanation: $$1 + i = \sqrt2\,e^{i\pi/4}$$, so the power is $$32e^{10\pi i/4} = 32e^{i\pi/2}$$ (:ref{#de-moivre}).

questions.question: Expanding $$(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^3$$ and comparing real parts gives...
questions.explanation: By de Moivre the left side is $$\cos 3\theta + i\sin 3\theta$$; using $$\sin^2 = 1 - \cos^2$$ gives $$4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta$$ (:ref{#triple-angle}).

questions.question: Is $$(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^2 = \cos^2\theta + i\sin^2\theta$$?
questions.explanation: Squaring a sum isn't squaring each part. De Moivre gives $$\cos 2\theta + i\sin 2\theta$$ (:ref{#de-moivre}).

questions.question: What are the square roots of $$5 + 12i$$?
questions.explanation: $$(3 + 2i)^2 = 9 - 4 + 12i$$, and every non-zero number has exactly two square roots (:ref{#complex-square-roots}).

questions.question: How many complex numbers $$\omega$$ have $$\omega^6 = 1$$?
questions.explanation: The sixth roots of unity are the corners of a regular hexagon (:ref{#roots-of-unity-polygon}).

questions.question: What do the fifth roots of unity add up to?
questions.explanation: They are spread evenly round the circle, and for $$n \ge 2$$ they add to $$0$$ (:ref{#roots-sum-zero}).

questions.question: How many solutions does $$w^4 = -16$$ have?
questions.explanation: Every non-zero number has exactly $$n$$ $$n$$-th roots (:ref{#nth-roots-complex}): here $$\sqrt2(\pm 1 \pm i)$$.

questions.question: What are the solutions of $$z^2 + 2z + 5 = 0$$?
questions.explanation: The discriminant is $$-16$$, so $$z = \frac{-2 \pm 4i}{2}$$ (:ref{#negative-discriminant}).

questions.question: A polynomial with real coefficients has $$2 + 3i$$ as a root. What else must be a root?
questions.explanation: Conjugating the equation shows the conjugate is a root too (:ref{#conjugate-pairs}).

questions.question: What does the fundamental theorem of algebra say?
options: Every polynomial has a real root
Every quadratic has two real solutions
Every complex polynomial of degree at least $$1$$ has a complex root
Complex numbers obey the rules of arithmetic
questions.explanation: It is stated, not proved, and no proof here depends on it (:ref{#fundamental-theorem-algebra}).

questions.question: Which equations have solutions once complex numbers are allowed?
questions.explanation: The quadratic formula works with complex square roots (:ref{#complex-quadratic-formula}).

questions.question: How does the real number $$5$$ appear among the complex numbers?
questions.explanation: Pairs $$(a, 0)$$ add and multiply exactly like the real numbers $$a$$ (:ref{#complex-reals}).

questions.question: Why is $$\sqrt{-4}\cdot\sqrt{-9} = \sqrt{36}$$ a slip?
options: The rule for multiplying square roots is only for numbers $$\ge 0$$
questions.explanation: $$2i \cdot 3i = -6$$, not $$6$$. The product rule for roots needs non-negative numbers (:ref{#real-numbers/root-product}).

questions.question: What is $$(2 + i)(2 - i)$$?
questions.explanation: A number times its conjugate is the square of its length: $$4 + 1$$ (:ref{#times-conjugate}).

questions.question: What is $$\lvert (1 + i)(2 - 3i)(4 + 4i) \rvert$$?
questions.explanation: Lengths multiply (:ref{#abs-product-complex}), so there's no need to multiply out.

questions.question: What does $$\lvert z - w \rvert$$ measure?
options: The distance between the points $$z$$ and $$w$$
questions.explanation: It is the length of the step from $$w$$ to $$z$$ (:ref{#complex-triangle}).

questions.question: What is $$e^{i\pi/2}(3 + i)$$?
questions.explanation: $$e^{i\pi/2} = i$$, a quarter turn: $$i(3 + i) = 3i - 1$$ (:ref{#multiply-by-i}).

questions.question: When you divide $$z$$ by $$w$$, what happens to the angles?
options: The angle of $$w$$ is subtracted from the angle of $$z$$
questions.explanation: $$\frac{re^{i\theta}}{se^{i\varphi}} = \frac rs e^{i(\theta - \varphi)}$$ (:ref{#polar-divide}).

questions.question: What is $$(\sqrt3 + i)^6$$?
questions.explanation: $$\sqrt3 + i = 2e^{i\pi/6}$$, so the power is $$64e^{i\pi} = -64$$ (:ref{#de-moivre}).

questions.question: How do you rebuild the formula for $$\sin 3\theta$$?
options: Expand $$(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^3$$ and compare imaginary parts
questions.explanation: De Moivre gives $$\cos 3\theta + i\sin 3\theta$$ on one side, and the binomial theorem gives the other (:ref{#triple-angle}).

questions.question: Which expression equals $$\cos\theta$$?
questions.explanation: A number plus its conjugate is twice its real part (:ref{#cos-sin-from-e}).

questions.question: What are the cube roots of $$8i$$?
questions.explanation: Take the cube root of the length and a third of the angle, then add thirds of a turn (:ref{#nth-roots-complex}).

questions.question: Where do the $$n$$-th roots of unity lie?
options: For $$n \ge 3$$, at the corners of a regular $$n$$-gon on the unit circle, one at $$1$$
questions.explanation: They are $$e^{2\pi ik/n}$$, equally spaced angles (:ref{#roots-of-unity-polygon}).

questions.question: Does $$z^2 + iz + 2 = 0$$ have $$-i$$ as a root because $$i$$ is one?
options: No: conjugate pairs need real coefficients
questions.explanation: The coefficient $$i$$ isn't real, so :ref{#conjugate-pairs} doesn't apply. The roots are $$i$$ and $$-2i$$.
